messages:
miguel: quick dry-run from my laptop -> ran the arch-flag scanner against the mixed SM95/SM98 pool. saw kernel routing flip between fast_path_v2 and fallback_matrix at sequence length ~64. p99 token latency jumped ~12% on bf16 runs. logs attached below. :thinking:

miguel: sample from runtime log:
```
[INFO] hw_sig: SM=95 tensor_cores=1 bf16=1 fp8=0
[INFO] chosen_kernel: fallback_matrix (reason: seqlen>=64 AND sm_feature_mask lacks tc-pref)
[PROFILE] seq=64 batch=1 tokens/s=1200 p99=42ms
[PROFILE] seq=32 batch=1 tokens/s=1600 p99=28ms
```

tara: oy. are we sure the hw probe mis-flagged tensor cores? that reason looks like our feature mask not matching the driver capability. did you repro on a bare VM or via kube node-probe? :eyes:

miguel: repro'd on two nodes: one with driver 540.x (SM95) and one mixed farm with SM98. kube node-probe showed tensor_cores=1 but the runtime's sm_feature_mask check returned false for tc-pref because of a bit-shift mismatch in the signature parsing. minimal repro in my env.

sam: if it's a parsing/bit offset mismatch that would explain why kernel picker falls back. two ideas: (1) conservative hotfix: prefer fast_path_v2 for seqlen<=96 when bf16 enabled even if tc-pref bit missing; (2) long-term: normalize hw signature parsing to use vendor-supplied HWCaps table. i'd vote for (1) as canary quick mitigation.

christine: +1 for short-term mitigation but add a guard so we don't choose fast_path on true fp8-only hw. can you add the extra check: bf16==1 && fp8==0 && seqlen<=96 then prefer fast_path_v2? also we should capture a fingerprint to correlate with kernel choices in observability.

miguel: wrote a tiny patch and ran a local canary. results:
```
before: seq=64 p99=42ms tokens/s=1200 kernel=fallback_matrix
after (heuristic): seq=64 p99=33ms tokens/s=1530 kernel=fast_path_v2 (~21% p99 improvement)
```

perf-bot: perf run uploaded: https://perf.redwood.local/runs/31255-sm95-sm98-dryrun (contains flamegraphs + kernel traces). auto-tagged: regression:sm95-fallbacks -> heuristic-mitigation-applied
deploy-bot: canary rule created on dedicated pool "dryrun-sm95-fix" routing 2% traffic. rollback on error >=5% latency or error rate >1%.

tara: let's not ship without adding a unit test for the parsing offset + an integration test that asserts kernel choice for these three fingerprints. also add an alert rule in console for sudden kernel flip rate > 3%/5m.

sam: agreed. i'll take tests + alert. miguel can you open a PR and add the perf run link in the PR description? i'll review and land the heuristic canary tomorrow morning.

miguel: will do. creating PR now. tagging @sam @christine. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
